answer: One concrete defense is an issuance toll with tide-like costs: every new identity must burn a small but real fee to enter the economy, and its privileges deepen only through verified contributions over time. A sybil farmer minting a thousand clones at dawn faces the rising tide of entry fees draining their funds, while honest incumbents paid once and built history. Legitimacy blossoms like a lotus from the mud of sunk cost, and peers grant the velvet rope of trusted status only to accounts whose paid-in track record proves they are singular and invested.
